# Teacher notes and illustrative answers
Separate teacher file; not access-protected. Original classroom draft 14 October 2026.
Lesson 1: switch primarily L2 within VLAN; router L3 across prefixes; AP bridges wireless to LAN; gateway is host routing role; modem/service termination handles access signalling; firewalls may inspect several layers. Star localises access-link faults but central switch/uplink remains a failure point. Assess final diagram against the specified Cisco symbol conventions, not just the concept rectangles.
Lesson 2: gateways .1/.65/.97/.113 on the routed firewall; VLANs 10/20/30/40; ordinary capacities 62/30/14/14. Staff may initiate IPP TCP 631 to printer .98, Visitors may not initiate internal flows. All unlisted new cross-zone connections denied. Offline web is TCP 443 only; realistic HTTP/3, infrastructure, stateful replies and management need explicit modelling/configuration. Same-VLAN flows can bypass the central firewall. Check actual enforcement location.
Lesson 3: demand 160 Mbit/s; ratio 1.6 or 160%; ideal share 5 Mbit/s; 400 MB x8 /100=32s ideal minimum. 1 Gbit/s local uplink has 160/1000=16% demand, but 100 Mbit/s internet still cannot carry the 160 Mbit/s if all crosses it. Overhead/storage/server/airtime/competing load limit observed rates. QoS redistributes priority, not total capacity.
Lesson 4: log A received 3/4:25% unanswered in this small sample; successful RTT mean 4 ms, not including timeout as zero. Cannot prove sustained 25% path loss. B hop 2 unanswered but destination responds: no proof forwarding failed. C IP responds but name unresolved: investigate DNS/record/client config, while IP and web health remain distinct. D ping succeeds but web fails: inspect service/transport/TLS/policy; ICMP success alone insufficient. E guest ping blocked: consistent with policy but does not prove all protocols/paths blocked.
Suggested formative review (not an official assessment): requirements and symbols; accurate addressing/segmentation; narrow policy/dependencies; correct units/bottleneck arithmetic; positive and negative tests; evidence limits and justified revision. Keep live-tool practice pending when only logs are used. Four lessons, no additional major project.
